atoms.b: Reptiles are ((warm-blooded ++cold-blooded)) creatures. That means that their body temperature takes the temperature of its environment. Their bodies are ((cold ++warm)) in the sun but ((warmer ++colder)) in the shade.
atoms.sound: Reptiles are cold-blooded creatures. That means that their body temperature takes the temperature of its environment. Their bodies are warm in the sun but colder in the shade.

atoms.b: Typical reptiles include ((tigers ++lizards)), crocodiles, turtles and ((sheep ++snakes)). Dinosaurs also belonged to the class of reptiles, before they became extinct.
atoms.sound: Typical reptiles include lizards, crocodiles, turtles and snakes. Dinosaurs also belonged to the class of reptiles, before they became extinct.

atoms.b: Most reptiles have ((++four three five)) legs and a tail.
atoms.sound: Most reptiles have four legs and a tail.

atoms.b: The skin of reptiles is covered with countless small, hard ((++scales hairs)).
atoms.sound: The skin of reptiles is covered with countless small, hard scales.

atoms.b: Some reptiles, like the ((++tortoise frog)), even have a solid shell.
atoms.sound: Some reptiles, like the tortoise, even have a solid shell.

atoms.b: As their scales don’t grow, reptiles need to ((++shed garage)) their skin regularly. Old scales fall off, while new, bigger scales form in their place.
atoms.sound: As their scales don’t grow, reptiles need to shed their skin regularly. Old scales fall off, while new, bigger scales form in their place.

instruction.text: Most reptiles lay eggs. Can you identify which animal is hatching in the pictures? Match the baby animals with the adult animals.
Which reptile matches the description? Choose the right answer.

atoms.a: It has a solid shell. Some of them can live up to 150 years.
It is big and green, has sharp teeth and lives in swamps.
It has a long, thin body, but no arms or legs.
This reptile can change its skin color.
